related.title: Jensen Huang says Nvidia will sell twice as many chips next year

cards.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said on Thursday that the company will double the number of chips it sells next year. It's the latest forecast from Nvidia that points to continuing massive growth for the next six quarters, and comes shortly after the company revealed that it expected 70% growth in the fiscal year ending in January 2028, or about $673 billion, which caused analyst expectations to shoot up. "I expect Nvidia to sell twice as many chips as this next year as we do this year," Huang told the media at a summit with King Charles III in Scotland. "The reason for that is because AI has, has so much contribution to the benefits of different industries, different economies, and you can see that in almost every single country that we're in, people want to invest in AI." Nvidia doesn't disclose the number of chips it sells in total. Its best-known products are its data center graphics processing units, or GPUs, such as its Blackwell and Rubin chips. Last fall, Huang said that Nvidia had shipped 6 million Blackwell GPUs in four quarters. But Nvidia makes a variety of semiconductors in addition to its GPUs, including central processors, or CPUs, switch chips, chips for optical networking, chips for laptops, Jetson chips for robots and cars, and the chip inside Nintendo's Switch 2 gaming console. Huang, who was joined at the summit by representatives from Google DeepMind, OpenAI and Anthropic, was in the U.K. to discuss AI safety, a topic that he's repeatedly weighed in on in recent weeks The public discourse over risks to humanity has reached a fever pitch after AI researchers warned that humans are no longer able to control the most advanced artificial intelligence. "When a product is not safe, we should hold it back and keep engineering it," Huang said.

cards.body: Nvidia Expects Chip Sales to Double in 2027 Jensen Huang just told a Scotland audience something about 2027 chip demand that sent analyst models scrambling and put NVIDIA's stock within striking distance of an all-time high. This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them. Shares of NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA | NVDA Price Prediction) are trading higher Thursday, up 2% to $219 in late-morning trading, after CEO Jensen Huang told an audience at a Scotland tech gathering that chip sales in 2027 are projected to roughly double compared to 2026. The move puts the stock back within reach of its 52-week high of $236. Huang Signals a Doubling in 2027 Chip Sales Huang confirmed at the event that shipment and sales volumes are expected to increase twofold next year, echoing what management already told investors on the August 26, 2026 earnings call. On that call, the CFO said “Customers’ forecasts point to our growth doubling next year” and framed the fiscal 2028 outlook, which calls for roughly 70% revenue growth, as “a supply-constrained outlook.” Huang added that “The unconstrained is significant.” The doubling narrative is being driven by the Vera Rubin platform, which entered full production alongside continued Blackwell deployment. Vera Rubin is expected to be “the fastest product ramp in NVIDIA’s history,” with per-gigawatt revenue opportunity rising to roughly $40 billion, up from $25 billion on Blackwell. Huang also stressed at the Scotland event that AI safety is paramount and that unsafe products should be withheld from the market. Supply Commitments and Sovereign AI Are Locking In Demand The demand backdrop is visible in NVIDIA’s own balance sheet. Supply obligations swelled to $279.0 billion, largely tied to memory procurement for Vera Rubin, per NVIDIA’s most recent 8-K filing. Management also disclosed guarantee obligations capped at $108.5 billion for AI cloud partners and said financing platforms with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR are expected to mobilize over $500 billion of third-party capital for AI infrastructure. Sovereign and enterprise AI, which Huang calls the invisible half of the business, is “growing 100% a year.” Sovereign AI revenue alone grew 35% sequentially and more than tripled year over year. Neocloud partners are expected to exit the year with eight gigawatts of installed capacity, versus roughly three gigawatts at the end of 2025. AWS is deploying an additional 2 million GPUs through fiscal 2029, and OpenAI’s existing and planned commitments now represent roughly 12 gigawatts of NVIDIA compute. All those gigawatts have to be powered, cooled, and networked by somebody, which is why we profiled seven of those suppliers in a free AI infrastructure report. Forecast Trend Report by Period Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang said semiconductor unit sales next year will double from this year as investment in artificial intelligence expands. Huang made the remarks to reporters ahead of the AI Summit in Scotland hosted by King Charles III, CNBC and other media outlets reported on September 17. "AI is making a very large contribution across industries and the broader economy," Huang said. Nvidia is seeing moves to invest in AI in nearly every country where it operates, he added. The forecast refers to semiconductor unit volumes, not revenue. Because prices differ by product, a doubling in sales volume would not necessarily produce the same rate of revenue growth. Nvidia does not separately disclose its total semiconductor unit sales. Nvidia’s product lineup includes data-center graphics processing units, or GPUs, as well as central processing units, switches and optical-networking semiconductors, laptop chips, and Jetson chips for robots and automobiles. When Nvidia reported second-quarter earnings on August 26, it projected fiscal 2028 revenue of about $673 billion, up 70% from a year earlier. Huang’s latest comments are also bolstering expectations that AI infrastructure investment will continue to expand across countries and industries. cards.body: 두산이 인공지능(AI) 데이터센터용 동박적층판(CCL) 생산능력 확대에 9684억원을 투자한다고 17일 공시했다. 지난해 연결기준 자기자본의 7.92%다. CCL은 인쇄회로기판(PCB)의 핵심소재다. 국내에 약 4210억원을 투입해 광모듈용 CCL 생산라인을 증설한다. 두산 전자BG는 현재 충북 증평, 경북 김천, 전북 익산·김제 등에 CCL 생산거점을 두고 있다. 중국에는 약 5474억원을 들여 AI 가속기와 네트워크 스위치용 CCL 공장을 신축한다. 두산이 지분 100%를 보유한 두산일렉트로머티리얼즈 창수 법인을 통해 투자한다. 이번 투자를 위해 창수 법인에 약 1824억원을 증자한다. 오는 2028년까지 3년에 걸쳐 단계적으로 투자를 집행한다. 2028년 하반기 가동을 시작한다. 이번 증설은 AI 데이터센터 투자 확대에 따른 고성능 CCL 수요가 배경이다. 올해 상반기 증평과 김천 공장 가동률은 각각 109.8%, 102.7%다. 중국 공장도 92.2% 가동률을 기록했다. 광모듈용 CCL 수요가 빠르게 늘었다. 올해 2분기 두산의 광모듈용 CCL 매출은 약 500억원으로 전년 대비 10배 이상이다. 광모듈용 CCL은 AI 데이터센터의 서버와 스위치 등을 연결해 대용량 데이터를 고속으로 전송하는 광통신 모듈 내 PCB 소재로 사용된다. 엔비디아 블랙웰와 루빈 등에 공급하는 AI 가속기용 CCL 수요도 급증했다. AI 가속기용 제품 등이 포함된 네트워크 보드용 CCL 매출은 올해 2분기 3692억원을 기록했다. 전자BG 전체 매출 절반 이상이다. 두산은 앞서 1800억원을 투자해 태국 사뭇쁘라깐주 방보 지역에 CCL 신규 공장 설립을 결정했다. 연내 착공해 2028년 하반기 양산이 목표다. 태국 공장까지 가동하면 두산의 CCL 생산거점은 한국, 중국에 이어 동남아시아까지 확대된다.

cards.body: Nvidia, Google and Emerald AI launch flexible data center consortium Nvidia Corp., Google LLC and software startup Emerald AI Inc. have formed an industry consortium to promote the construction of flexible data centers. The AI Energy Management Alliance, or AEMA, officially launched on Wednesday. A flexible data center is a facility that cuts its power draw when the electrical grid is under strain. That usage reduction can take multiple forms. If household energy demand is expected to peak in the afternoon on a certain day, data center operators can schedule their AI training runs to avoid that time frame. Alternatively, they can draw power from on-site batteries instead of the grid. Onsite batteries also have other benefits. If a utility is struggling to meet consumer demand on its own, data center operators can inject some of their stored electricity into the grid. The AEMA’s three founding members are closely involved in the flexible data center ecosystem. Google has developed what it calls demand response technologies to align its cloud facilities’ energy usage with grid requirements. In March, the company disclosed that its demand response capacity exceeds 1 gigawatt. Nvidia offers a software tool called DSX Flex to data center operators that use its Rubin graphics cards. The application can optimize an AI facility’s grid usage, on-premise energy generation equipment and batteries. It makes optimization decisions based partly on signals from power utilities’ infrastructure. Emerald AI, the third founding member of AEMA, is a startup that raised $150 million in funding last month. It counts Nvidia among its investors. The two companies are collaborating on a 100-megawatt data center in Manassas, Virginia that they describe as the “world’s first power-flexible AI factory.” Emerald AI offers a software platform called Emerald Conductor that enables server clusters to lower their energy consumption when the grid is under stress. According to the company, the software also limits the impact of power draw reductions on AI workloads. Emerald Conductor will be used in the Manassas data center that Emerald AI is building with Nvidia. AEMA is also backed by 18 other companies. The group includes Anthropic PBC, chipmaker Analog Devices Inc. and multiple utilities. The consortium’s first priority will be to develop best practices for flexible data centers. According to AEMA, its best practices will cover details such as how facilities should respond to power outages. The goal is to encourage data center builders to implement those standards in new facilities before they’re powered on. AEMA’s work will also cover other areas. It will seek to standardize the metrics that data center operators use to evaluate their power optimization efforts. cards.body: Nvidia-backed CoreWeave said Thursday it plans to raise $3 billion through a convertible debt offering, highlighting the massive funding needs to support the buildout of AI infrastructure. Initial buyers of the debt may purchase up to an additional $500 million. CoreWeave said it would use some of the proceeds to protect against dilution, while the remainder would fund its operations. The company also launched an at-the-market stock sale program for up to 35 million shares, potentially raising about $2.92 billion based on Wednesday’s closing price. However, CoreWeave will determine whether to sell shares based on market conditions. READ: Meta deepens ties with CoreWeave with $21 billion deal (April 10, 2026) The program is being managed by Deutsche Bank, Goldman Sachs and JP Morgan and is part of CoreWeave’s efforts to move toward an investment-grade credit profile. Shares of the company plunged more than 2% in premarket trading Thursday. Through Wednesday’s close, the stock had gained more than 16% so far this year. CoreWeave also said that it signed short-term customer contracts for compute capacity in the third quarter at approximately $40 million per megawatt on an annualized basis. The company increased its contracted power capacity to about 4.2 gigawatts from 3.7 gigawatts at the end of June. CoreWeave reported a revenue backlog of $104.2 billion in the second quarter in August. The company later disclosed more than $25 billion in additional customer commitments signed early in the third quarter. READ: CoreWeave secures $8.5 billion loan for AI infrastructure expansion (March 31, 2026) In a press release Tuesday, CoreWeave said the short-term contracts signed in the third quarter span three to six months, with pricing calculated as annualized revenue divided by the power required to service the related clusters. The company said it has continued to contract new compute capacity at higher prices since June 30. CoreWeave also announced the establishment of an at-the-market offering program under which it may sell up to 35 million shares of Class A common stock from time to time. Earlier this year, Meta committed to spending $21 billion on AI cloud infrastructure from CoreWeave. This came in addition to a commitment for Meta to pay CoreWeave about $14.2 billion through Dec. 14, 2031, with an option to expand the agreement through 2032 for additional cloud computing capacity.

cards.body: Snap $SNAPannounced partnerships with Nvidia $NVDA, Amazon $AMZN Web Services, and Salesforce $CRM on Wednesday to bring its SPECS augmented reality glasses into workplace environments, targeting industries including retail, manufacturing, and field operations. The partnerships are designed to give workers hands-free access to information and AI-powered guidance while on the job. Salesforce is integrating its Agentforce platform with SPECS, allowing employees to identify objects, log issues, surface relevant data, and update workflows without switching to a separate screen. AWS is connecting SPECS to its Amazon Quick AI assistant, enabling workers to query inventory information and other workplace data directly through the glasses. Snap is working with Nvidia to bring agents built on Nvidia's XR AI platform to SPECS, allowing the glasses to interpret a worker's surroundings and deliver real-time guidance, the company said. Snap CEO Evan Spiegel said the Nvidia and Salesforce partnerships are aimed at making it easier for businesses to adopt existing agentic AI platforms through SPECS, according to CNBC. Spiegel framed the enterprise push in similar terms, telling CNBC it is part of the company's ongoing effort to shift public perception so people understand "that Specs is a computer, not a pair of smart glasses for taking photos." Two additional partners are also involved in the enterprise program. Tandem by Trifork connects on-site technicians with remote experts who can annotate the technician's field of view in real time, while Hololight turns SPECS into a spatial workstation with access to tools, documents, and 3D models via video streaming. Snap said it is also working with device management vendors to build mobile device management and security controls for enterprise deployments at scale. At the same event in Los Angeles, Snap introduced SPECS Intelligence, an AI service designed to work across SPECS glasses, iPhone, and Mac. The service is built to anticipate when assistance would be useful and surface relevant information without waiting for a user prompt. A preview is available today in the SPECS app for iOS in the United States; a fuller experience on Mac is available by invitation only. On pricing, Spiegel told CNBC that no final decisions have been made, though the service will offer a free tier alongside other tiers that vary by usage level. SPECS AR glasses are available to pre-order for $2,195, with shipping expected later this fall in the United States, United Kingdom, and France. A new SPECS Charging Case with Cellular, sold separately, is available through a partnership with Verizon $VZ for a bundle price of $2,395. Beginning October 1, consumers can try the glasses at a pop-up location at Westfield Century City in Los Angeles, the company said. cards.body: NVIDIA and Google's new coalition wants to speed up AI data center power grid connections In exchange, the facilities would reduce power usage during peak demand. NVIDIA, Google and Emerald AI have launched a new coalition called the AI Energy Management Alliance (AEMA), the companies announced. The aim is to promote more flexible AI data centers that won't be disruptive to electricity grids or require massive, taxpayer-funded upgrades. In exchange, the coalition wants utility operators to connect their data centers faster. As NVIDIA explains in its own blog post, US power infrastructure was built for "flat, static electricity demand" and not for computing centers that can moderate power usage. To that end, the companies want to set a standard for flexible data centers that can shift computing workloads, discharge storage and respond to system contingencies, making it a "controllable resource rather than an inflexible load." Emerald AI, a startup dedicated to making data centers more flexible, explained the new coalition's purpose in a Fortune article. New US data centers can wait a decade or more for a grid connection, because utilities need to ensure they have enough capacity to serve everyone when demand is highest, "including on sweltering afternoons when air conditioners are running full tilt," CEO Varun Sivaram wrote. At the same time, the grid is only 50 percent utilized on average, so if "AI data centers were flexible during the grid's worst hours of the year, America could unlock 100GW on our existing grid for flexible data centers." To that end, AEMA is suggesting principles like "setting clear rules for facilities regarding staying connected during brief grid disturbances, reducing power use when needed and responding to emergencies." Technical requirements, performance metrics and operational data sharing would also be standardized. As a tit-for-tat, grid operators would connect data centers to the grid more quickly while potentially sharing costs. Some of the technology the group is proposing are batteries that carry facilities through peaks, on-site generation to support demand and software than can "slow, pause or shift less urgent computing." The coalition is likely a response to a massive public backlash against AI data centers that politicians are starting to realize could affect their future electability. AEMA doesn't really address the massive amounts of pollution created by these data centers thanks to their energy demands, nor the noise and general disturbance to the neighboring communities. Rather, it wants to ensure that it gets data centers connected more quickly, in exchange for creating less of a hassle for regional electrical grids. To that end, it will also serve as a lobbying arm for big tech. "AEMA will press this case in state capitals and in Washington. headlines.body: American nonprofit C4ADS, a monitoring organization funded mostly by the U.S. government, produced a report shedding light on the many ways that American AI accelerators reach China. Somewhat paradoxically, the U.S. refuses to sell advanced AI chips to China, while simultaneously the CCP prohibits their purchase, but that has seemingly not stopped the products from arriving on Eastern shores. C4ADS's report identifies three major avenues for chip smuggling: direct acquisitions via research institutions, drop-shipping through other Southeast Asian countries, and purchases through a matryoshka-doll-like structure made of shell companies. The writers note that only explicitly mentioned chips are accounted for, meaning the actual amount of hardware changing hands could be far higher. Another earlier report by Epoch AI estimates that around a third (and possibly most of) China's AI compute power is comprised of smuggled GPUs. Firstly, a quick primer on chip logistics. Nvidia has most of its chips manufactured and packaged at TSMC in Taiwan. An individual chip, or the entire accelerator unit it's in, might go through several rounds of testing, potentially doing more than one trip before it lands in a customer's data center. As for export and import controls: the U.S. forbids the sale of H100, A100, and Blackwell-family chips to China; the lower-end H20 chip and the meatier H200 (and AMD MI325X) can be traded on a case-by-case basis, with the latter getting a 25% tariff. Meanwhile, China's broad position is to discourage and restrict the purchase of American AI chips, in a bid to spur its national efforts, currently spearheaded by Huawei . However, multiple reports indicate the authorities often turn a blind eye to gray/black-market imports, and 2026 saw official exceptions issued to ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent . The first way to get a 'forbidden' chip into China via quasi-legal means is by simply getting a Chinese university or research institution to buy it. These entities reportedly include Nvidia GPUs inside "sprawling multi-vendor contracts," routed through small Chinese regional integrators. The report also claims that some buyer institutions have ties to the CCP and the country's defense and intelligence sectors. C4ADS says that it tracked 56 chips worth $1.7 million sold this way in the report's July 2025 to January 2026 period. Additionally, it says that its 2024 investigation covering multiple years of government records revealed $6.48 million worth of silicon heading to China in this manner. The second route for smuggling potent silicon is technically legal, via drop-shipping it through Southeast Asian countries including Vietnam, India, and Malaysia. C4ADS analyzed transactions between 2022 and 2025, and found $13.4 million of Nvidia A100, H100/GH100, and AD102-series GPUs routed through the aforementioned countries, in a "consistent pattern." headlines.body: Grid software unicorn Emerald AI has formed a coalition with Google and Nvidia that will use the startup’s technology to secure space on the grid for more data centers. The AI Energy Management Alliance (AEMA) hopes to make demand response — a paradigm in which data centers temporarily reduce their electricity use — an integral part of data center development. Pausing noncritical tasks and shifting some compute loads, AEMA says, could allow an additional 100 gigawatts of data centers to connect to the grid. The founding trio is joined by Anthropic, and a range of utilities including AES, Constellation, National Grid, and NRG Energy. Demand response is an old concept that has been used by utilities for decades. It works because the grid is designed with peak loads in mind. For much of the year, demand is well below the maximum the grid can support. Traditionally, demand response covered large electricity users like factories, which in times of high demand would agree to reduce their usage, typically by pausing production or switching to backup generators. In exchange, the utility would pay them for the service, often handsomely. Today, data centers can also take advantage of those programs, usually by turning on backup generators. Emerald AI has been proposing an alternative to dirty diesel generators. The company’s software coordinates requests from utilities with data centers, which can pause noncritical tasks or shift loads to other data centers where the grid has some headroom. The startup isn’t the only one working on such technology. Google has been developing its own tools, and Enel X lets data centers tap their uninterruptible power supplies to round off peaks in power demand. Limiting max grid usage to 90% for a few hours at a time could let data centers free up 76 gigawatts of capacity, according to a study by Goldman Sachs published last year. Emerald AI does have an advantage, though. Its software connects utilities directly to data centers, which should allow data centers to respond quickly to requests, much like batteries. The startup also recently raised $150 million in a Series A led by Energize Capital and DCVC, giving it the sort of funding needed to roll out the technology on a wider scale. Given the peaky nature of AI compute loads, and data centers’ ability to quickly ramp up and down, the creation of something like AEMA is overdue. The coalition also promises to help tech companies and utilities find new sites for data centers, an effort that hasn’t been easy for either party. Despite its promise, more sophisticated demand response won’t solve all of the grid’s problems today. Ayse Coskun, Emerald AI’s chief scientist, told TechCrunch that her company’s technology promises to blunt the industry’s need for new generating sources, but it won’t eliminate it entirely.

headlines.body: Google, Nvidia, and AI orchestration firm Emerald AI have launched the AI Energy Management Alliance (AEMA) to support the development of flexible load capabilities within the AI data center sector. The founding members were joined by a range of launch partners across the data center and energy sectors. These include Anthropic, The AES Corporation, Constellation, Generate, National Grid, NRG Energy, Analog Devices, Calibrant Energy, Camus, ClearPath, encoord, Fluence, GridUnity, PassKey Inc., RWE, Splight, Verrus, and Voltus. Writing on LinkedIn, Tyler Norris, head of energy market innovation – AI & infrastructure, said: “Our shared mission: modernize power system planning and operations for the 21st century to unlock the full potential of flexible data centers, enabling digital infrastructure to actively enhance system utilization, affordability, and reliability. “Instead of waiting 5-7+ years for traditional system upgrades, multiple studies have found that reducing net grid withdrawal for less than 100 hours per year can unlock dozens of gigawatts of capacity via compute flexibility, storage, or generation. At Google, we’ve proven this model by integrating 1GW of demand response capacity nationwide.” In support of the AEMA, Google has released two new reports setting out actionable pathways forward. They include a report from The Brattle Group, which provides a technical blueprint to turn recent bipartisan direction from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission into operational reality. Alongside a report from Aurora Energy Research, which models flexible data centers in ERCOT paired with front-of-meter resources. Norris will serve as the AEMA's inaugural board chair. Data center demand response capabilities have become a hot topic in the sector, as operators seek to move from consumers to active grid participants. In March, Google reported that it had integrated a total of 1GW of demand response capacity into its long-term energy contracts with multiple utilities across the US. After originally demonstrating its demand-response capabilities with Omaha Public Power District in 2024, the company announced agreements with Indiana Michigan Power (I&M) and Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) last year. Google has now signed contracts with Entergy Arkansas, Minnesota Power, and DTE Energy that incorporate demand response.

The machines are expected to use M8 Ultra processors and arrive in 2029, the report claims. For now, the usage of the NVLink Fusion platform is not formalized and has not been confirmed by either Apple or Nvidia, but if Apple decides to use it instead of competing solutions, this may have significantly broader market implications than just Apple using Nvidia hardware. Apple looking for fast interconnects Apple is reportedly considering at least two server configurations: a smaller machine equipped with two M8 Ultra processors and a higher-end version featuring four M8 Ultra system-on-chips. Although Apple has its own UltraFusion technology for stitching two high-end SoCs together seamlessly, it looks like the company does not have a proper solution for scale-up and scale-out connectivity of its processors, which is where Nvidia's NVLink Fusion comes into play. Apparently, Apple wants to use NVLink infrastructure, which includes not only an interconnection protocol, but also switches, chiplets that add NVLink connectivity, and a software stack, for its servers. The project was reportedly initiated around a year ago and was backed by John Ternus while he headed Apple's hardware engineering organization. Apple already builds custom servers for Private Cloud Compute, which handle AI workloads too demanding for local execution on iPhones and Macs, The Information claims. Most of these machines use Apple's internally developed connectivity technologies, which are reportedly too slow and costly for large-scale commercial deployments, which is why Apple is looking elsewhere. More than NVLink? The Information specifically mentions Apple's need for connectivity technology suitable for large-scale deployments, although it does not explain exactly what this means architecturally. headlines.body: 네이버클라우드가 국책과제로 개발하는 보안 특화 인공지능(AI) 모델을 글로벌 시장으로 확산하겠다는 계획을 밝혔다. 김유원 네이버클라우드 대표는 17일 국가정보원과 국가보안기술연구소가 서울 코엑스에서 공동 주최한 사이버 서밋 코리아(CSK) 2026 기조연설자로 나와 "네이버클라우드는 최근 엔비디아와 함께 글로벌 AI 팩토리로의 도약을 선언했다"면서 "앞으로 세계 각지 AI 팩토리에서 AI 보안 모델이 함께 작동하도록 만들고 각 거점을 사이버 안보 협력 허브로 연결하겠다"고 말했다. 김 대표는 지난 6월 대만에서 열린 엔비디아 클라우드 파트너 서밋에서 글로벌 AI 팩토리 구축 계획을 공개한 바 있다. 젠슨 황 엔비디아 최고경영자(CEO)는 전날 GTC 타이베이 기조연설에서 네이버클라우드를 글로벌 AI 생태계 핵심 파트너로 소개했다. 7월에는 이해진 네이버 의장이 엔비디아와 브룩필드로부터 총 100억달러를 투자받는다고 발표했다. 엔비디아는 10억달러를 네이버에 전략적으로 투자하고 브룩필드는 최대 90억달러 규모의 AI 인프라 조달을 지원하는 구조다. 이날 김 대표 발언은 이런 협력 관계를 활용해 세계 시장으로 모델을 확산하겠다는 의미로 해석됐다. 네이버클라우드는 최근 정부의 사이버 보안 특화 AI 파운데이션 모델 개발 사업 수행기관으로 선정됐다. 오는 18일부터 개발을 시작한다. 사업은 한국의 보안 환경과 산업 현장을 학습한 AI 모델을 개발하는 것이 목표다. LG CNS 등과 컨소시엄을 꾸려 전력, 금융, 반도체, 방위산업 등 주요 산업 현장에서 모델을 실증할 계획이다. 김 대표는 이날 연설에서 AI 사이버 공격의 위협이 커졌다고 강조했다. 과거에는 취약점이 발견된 뒤 실제 공격으로 이어지기까지 수십일, 길게는 수개월이 걸렸지만 AI가 취약점을 찾고 공격 방법까지 만들어내면서 이 시간이 수십분 수준까지 줄어들고 있다고 했다. 김 대표는 "사람이 밤 새워 분석하고 대응책을 만드는 동안 공격은 이미 끝나 있을 수 있다"며 "사람의 속도로 AI의 공격을 막는 시대는 끝나가고 있다"고 말했다. 개별 기업이나 국가 단위 대응만으로는 AI를 활용한 사이버 공격을 막기 어렵다고도 했다. 김 대표는 "AI가 가져올 위험을 어느 한 조직이 혼자 해결할 수 없다"며 "공격자에게 국경은 없고 방어에도 국경이 있어선 안 된다"고 말했다. 이어 "AI 시대에 방어는 몇 개의 폐쇄된 시스템으로 만들어질 수 없다"며 "누구나 검증하고 활용할 수 있어야 하고 각 기업의 강점을 연결하는 생태계가 필수"라고 했다. 그는 "하나의 나라가 스스로를 지키는 것을 넘어 여러 나라가 서로를 지켜주는 구조를 만드는 것이 저희가 생각하는 국경을 넘어선 연대"라고 말했다. 네이버는 이미 국제 보안 기구 등과 협력을 하고 있다. 나토 사이버방위협력센터(CCDCOE)가 주관하는 국제 사이버 방어훈련 록드쉴즈(Locked Shields)에 한국 연합팀 일원으로 2년 연속 참가했다. 엔비디아가 주도하는 오픈 시큐어 AI 얼라이언스(Open Secure AI Alliance)에도 참여 중이다. 김 대표는 "네이버클라우드가 자체 보안 역량에 연간 400억원 이상을 투입하고 100명이 넘는 보안 전문인력을 운영하고 있다"면서 "관련 투자는 지속 확대할 계획"이라고 밝혔다.

headlines.body: 소셜미디어 서비스 '스냅챗'의 운영사 스냅(Snap)이 300만원(2195달러)대의 증강현실(AR) 글래스 '스펙스(Specs)'를 16일(현지 시각) 출시했다. 이를 위해 스냅은 앞서 엔비디아, AWS, 세일즈포스 등과 파트너십을 체결했다. 스냅이 스펙스를 출시한 배경은 또 다른 형태의 기업용 컴퓨팅 장비 시장 진출이다. 스펙스는 지난 6월 발표됐다. 당시 스냅은 스펙스를 새로운 종류의 컴퓨터로 소개하면서 인공지능(AI) 지원, 업무 도구, 엔터테인먼트와 함께 협업도 언급했다. 2195달러는 일반 소비자가 구매하기에 진입 장벽으로 작용한다. 반면 기업은 현장 작업자의 생산성 향상을 위한 설비 투자로 가능하다. 회사는 스펙스를 업무용 컴퓨터로 활용하도록 하는 것에 목적을 둔다. 매장이나 서비스 현장은 물론, 공장이나 제조 시설도 대상이다. 스펙스는 컴퓨팅 하드웨어를 안경 자체에 넣었고(독립형 AR 기기) 외부 배터리팩이나 별도의 컴퓨팅 장치(puck), 케이블 연결이 필요 없다. 작업자가 스마트폰이나 노트북을 꺼내지 않고 눈앞에서 정보를 확인하고 음성·손동작으로 업무를 처리하도록 해준다. 스냅에 따르면 스펙스에서 세일즈포스의 자율형 AI 에이전트 구축 플랫폼 '에이전트포스'를 사용해 문제를 확인하고 관련 정보를 조회하거나 업무를 처리할 수 있다. AWS의 업무용 에이전틱 AI 어시스턴트 플랫폼 '아마존 퀵(Amazon Quick)'과 연결해 작업자는 음성으로 재고·제품 위치 등 정보를 조회할 수 있도록 할 계획이다. 또 엔비디아는 'XR AI 스택(NVIDIA XR AI Stack)' 기반 에이전트가 작업자의 주변 환경과 기업 데이터를 이해하고 실시간 안내할 수 있는 기술을 지원한다. 또 엔지니어링 기업 트라이포크, 산업용 AR/VR 소프트웨어 기업 홀로라이트와도 협력한다. 트라이포크는 현장 기술자와 원격 전문가·AI 에이전트를 연결하고, 홀로라이트는 문서·3D 모델 등을 AR 공간에서 사용하는 작업 환경을 제공한다. 에반 스피겔(Evan Spiegel) 스냅 CEO는 "기존 AR 기기의 투박하고 큰 디자인이 활용을 가로막는 주요 요인이었다"고 지적했다. 스펙스는 무게 132~136g이며 퍽, 케이블 없이 독립적으로 작동한다. 이는 현장 엔지니어가 디지털 지침을 보며 장비를 점검하거나 작업자·원격 전문가와 소통하는 업무에 AR 글래스 활용을 보다 쉽게 할 수 있다는 설명이다. 또 스냅은 아이폰, 맥용 AI 어시스턴트 '스펙스 인텔리전스(Specs Intelligence)'도 선보였다. 가격 정책은 확정 전으로, 스피겔 CEO는 무료부터 다양한 가격대의 요금제를 사용량 기준으로 제공할 것으로 전했다. 스냅은 2016년 카메라가 탑재된 스마트 안경 '스펙터클스(Spectacles)'를 선보인 이후 AR 글래스 기술을 꾸준히 개발해왔다. 실제 공간에 AR 콘텐츠를 띄울 수 있는 디스플레이형 스펙터클스(2021년), 독립형 AR 글래스와 전용 운영체제 '스냅 OS'(2024년) 등을 발표했다. 자체 광학엔진과 공간인식 기술까지 개발하는 등 AR 글래스의 선두주자로 자리매김해 왔다.

headlines.body: Posting this for discussion/awareness, not asking for tech support on my own card (I've got that covered). Blackwell GPUs (RTX 5070/5080/5090, RTX PRO 6000) have a recurring failure where the GPU randomly falls off the PCIe bus — full lockup, zero warning, only a hard power cycle recovers it. Kernel log shows Xid 79 (sometimes Xid 120/154 too), and it doesn't come back on a warm reboot. On July 14, 2026, an NVIDIA employee ("amrits", a forum moderator) confirmed on NVIDIA's own developer forums that this is a known internal issue, tracked as bug 6426268: "We have seen similar issue internally and is currently being investigated via internal bug 6426268." That's 10 weeks ago as of today. Since then: no public root-cause statement, no workaround, no ETA. Meanwhile the tracking thread on NVIDIA's own GitHub repo has grown to 35+ independent reports across multiple GPU models, multiple driver branches (580/595/610), and both Linux and Windows: github.com/NVIDIA/open-gpu-kernel-modules/issues/1151 The community has independently ruled out PSU, thermals, PCIe seating/cabling, and even a full motherboard swap on individual cards — which points at GSP firmware rather than anyone's specific build. Several reporters also describe the time between crashes shrinking with continued use. I'm one of the affected owners (RTX 5080) and have a full report/logs in that GitHub thread. Curious how many people here are hitting this that haven't found the GitHub issue or forum thread yet — feels like it's more widespread than the report count suggests, and more visibility might get NVIDIA to actually respond. submitted by /u/Upstairs_Ride6714 [link] [comments]
